content:
No — not unless you're facing a hard regulatory or product-capability ceiling you can't route around.
Replatforming core banking is the highest-risk, longest-duration bet in financial services technology. The failure rate on full replacements is well-documented, and the organizations that come out ahead are almost always the ones that had no realistic alternative — their legacy platform genuinely couldn't support the business model they needed to run.
The more common and more defensible path is strangling the monolith: wrapping the core with modern API layers, migrating products and customer segments incrementally, and deferring the full replacement until the new platform has proven itself under real load.
